competencies.name: abstraction / systematic generalization (relational, PARTIAL)
competencies.description: go to the goal whose colour-vector is most similar to the cue's; the comparison PARTIALLY transfers to colours never seen as a cue-match in training
competencies.mechanism: go to the goal whose colour-vector is most similar to the cue's; the comparison PARTIALLY transfers to colours never seen as a cue-match in training
competencies.diagnostic: TRAIN vs HELD-OUT colour split (a generalization gap, NOT an ablation): held-out colours appear only as DISTRACTORS in training. held-out-acc 0.59 vs chance 0.33 => genuine transfer; train 0.88 -> held-out 0.59 => +0.29 gap => INCOMPLETE. Pure per-instance memorization would leave held-out AT chance 0.33; it did not.
competencies.lit_name: systematic / compositional generalization; relational abstraction (Fodor-Pylyshyn systematicity; the well-documented 'nets generalize relations only PARTIALLY' finding, e.g. SCAN/Lake-Baroni)
competencies.state_required: n/a (feedforward MLP; the relation is computed per-step, no memory)
competencies.state_mode: a learned RELATION -- similarity(cue, each goal colour-vector) -- applied to HELD-OUT instances

competencies.name: imitation / social learning (goal emulation)
competencies.description: observe a scripted demonstrator that walks toward the hidden-correct goal; identify + go to the goal it chose (goal-emulation). The correct goal is NOT in the learner's observation -- the demonstrator is the only signal.
competencies.mechanism: observe a scripted demonstrator that walks toward the hidden-correct goal; identify + go to the goal it chose (goal-emulation). The correct goal is NOT in the learner's observation -- the demonstrator is the only signal.
competencies.diagnostic: FROZEN demonstrator (sits at centre, no behaviour to read) -> 0.08, BELOW chance 0.33 => the hidden goal is unfindable without the other agent. MISLEADING demonstrator (walks to a WRONG goal) -> 0.08 => the learner FOLLOWS it to the wrong goal, proving it copies the demonstrator's CHOICE (not another cue). needs-demonstrator +0.75; misled-by-demo +0.75.
competencies.metric: normal 0.83 vs frozen 0.08 vs mislead 0.08 (chance 0.33) -- the cleanest demand in the arc
competencies.lit_name: social / observational learning; goal emulation (Bandura 1977; Tomasello -- emulation vs true action-level imitation)
competencies.state_required: n/a (feedforward MLP; reads the demonstrator each step)
competencies.state_mode: another agent's BEHAVIOUR used as an information source about the (hidden) task goal

competencies.name: predictive intention-reading (velocity-based goal attribution) -- theory-of-mind component
competencies.description: integrate the mover's observed motion (start->stop) to recover its heading, then attribute its goal as the one in the heading direction. The 3 goals are EQUIDISTANT from the mover's frozen stop, so the single frame is provably SYMMETRIC and ONLY the motion identifies g*.
competencies.mechanism: integrate the mover's observed motion (start->stop) to recover its heading, then attribute its goal as the one in the heading direction. The 3 goals are EQUIDISTANT from the mover's frozen stop, so the single frame is provably SYMMETRIC and ONLY the motion identifies g*.
competencies.diagnostic: MEMORYLESS baseline PROVABLY at chance (0.32 -- symmetric single frame is an airtight control by construction) vs recurrent 0.86 => needs-memory +0.54. mover-FROZEN (sits at the stop, no motion) -> 0.32 chance => needs-mover +0.54.
competencies.lit_name: intention attribution / inverse planning / machine theory-of-mind (Baker 2009; Rabinowitz et al. 2018)
competencies.state_mode: integrated MOTION history of another agent -> inferred heading -> attributed goal (intention)

competencies.name: cumulative-culture ratchet (cross-generational)
competencies.description: each generation inherits the culture prefix, COPIES it (imitation) and explores the FRONTIER symbol (innovation); discoveries accumulate into the buffer, so the recipe is solved ACROSS generations, never within one
competencies.mechanism: each generation inherits the culture prefix, COPIES it (imitation) and explores the FRONTIER symbol (innovation); discoveries accumulate into the buffer, so the recipe is solved ACROSS generations, never within one
competencies.diagnostic: REMOVE the inherited culture buffer (no-inheritance) -> collapses 11.69/12 (97%) -> 0.38/12 (3%); needs-inheritance +11.31. A single generation cannot discover a random length-12 recipe (exponential); cross-generational accumulation can.
competencies.metric: cumulative 11.69/12 (97%) vs single-generation 0.38/12 (3%); ratchet gap +11.31 (confirmed @120 generations)
competencies.lit_name: cumulative cultural evolution / the ratchet effect (Tomasello; Boyd & Richerson; Henrich; Kirby iterated learning)
competencies.state_required: n/a -- the state is EXTERNALIZED in a persistent culture buffer that outlives any individual
competencies.state_mode: an accumulated cultural ARTIFACT (the known-correct recipe prefix) persisting across agent lifetimes

competencies.name: division of labor (anti-coordination / task allocation)
competencies.description: n homogeneous agents must reach n DISTINCT targets (perfect matching = division of labor); starting symmetric, they break symmetry into complementary roles anchored on agent identity, a behavior the openhunt-family substrate structurally CANNOT express (openhunt only rewards convergence to a shared target)
competencies.mechanism: n homogeneous agents must reach n DISTINCT targets (perfect matching = division of labor); starting symmetric, they break symmetry into complementary roles anchored on agent identity, a behavior the openhunt-family substrate structurally CANNOT express (openhunt only rewards convergence to a shared target)
competencies.diagnostic: ablation battery: memwipe (memoryless) and blind (no observation) both collapse it (load-bearing), and noid (zero own-identity one-hot) collapses it in expressing seeds (identity-anchored, noid mean necessity 0.66) -- the division-of-labor-specific channel. Within-episode: teleport one agent off its target mid-episode -> allocation breaks -> re-forms in ~90% of episodes (recovery 0.90), the self-repair signature of an actively maintained behavior
competencies.metric: within-episode (expressing seeds, alloc_dynamics 6 seeds/4 expressing): formation 0.64, occupancy (duty cycle) 0.88, recovery-from-perturbation 0.90, role-fluidity 0.02 (roles held). Across training seeds: DYNAMIC/non-permanent -- reliably discovered, but STABLY expressed in a variable fraction of seeds that rises with training quality: confirm (800 iters) 1/6=17%, deepen (2500) 3/6=50%, curriculum-scaffolded 4/6=67%; 2x budget alone did NOT raise it (long 1/3=33%), so across-seed variability is an optimization property, not under-training. novelty distance >=0.44 (range 0.44-0.53) from all 13 multi-channel known fingerprints
competencies.lit_name: emergent division of labor / self-organized task allocation / role specialization (Krieger 2000 ant-like robot task allocation; Berman 2009 optimal swarm allocation policies; Duarte 2012 & Ulrich 2018 self-organized DoL response-threshold/evolution; Zeng 2023 role-based MARL; Liu 2023 identity-aware MARL)
competencies.state_required: recurrent policy memory + per-agent identity; agents hold a role assignment across the episode
competencies.state_mode: an implicit role assignment (which agent covers which target) maintained through the episode and re-established after disruption

competencies.name: group-size regulation (homeostatic set-point tracking)
competencies.description: n agents each choose active/inactive; a shared reward peaks when the active count equals a time-varying target K*(t) that switches every few rounds across the full range [1,n-1]. Starting symmetric, agents break symmetry into a stable active subset anchored on identity, and re-regulate the count when the target moves or active members are knocked offline. First EPC substrate to express regulation toward a MOVING set-point (vs swarm-quorum's static detection or division-of-labor's fixed matching). Fully cooperative (shared reward), so it trains under independent PPO where the mixed-motive axis could not.
competencies.mechanism: n agents each choose active/inactive; a shared reward peaks when the active count equals a time-varying target K*(t) that switches every few rounds across the full range [1,n-1]. Starting symmetric, agents break symmetry into a stable active subset anchored on identity, and re-regulate the count when the target moves or active members are knocked offline. First EPC substrate to express regulation toward a MOVING set-point (vs swarm-quorum's static detection or division-of-labor's fixed matching). Fully cooperative (shared reward), so it trains under independent PPO where the mixed-motive axis could not.
competencies.diagnostic: ablation battery: noid (zero own-identity one-hot) collapses it fully (necessity 1.00, identity-anchored roles); blind (no view of others/count) 0.75, memwipe (memoryless) 0.75, mute (scrambled target signal) 0.74 all load-bearing. Within-episode knockout (force KNOCK_D active agents offline mid-episode): group re-regulates within ~1 round.
competencies.metric: trains 3/3 seeds to exact-match regulation 1.000, tracking error 0.000 (best fixed-count baseline only 0.256, so genuinely tracking the moving target). within-episode dynamics (size_dynamics, 3 seeds): formation 1.00, knockout-recovery 0.97-1.00, recovery_time ~1 round, natural-set-point-change re-hit ~0.77. internal novelty gate: min fingerprint distance 0.523 (to phase-align); swarm-quorum 0.636; division-of-labor not in top 6.
competencies.lit_name: homeostatic regulation of active-worker number / reserve labor force / response-threshold task allocation (Charbonneau 2017 inactive workers as reserve replacing removed active workers -- direct knockout-recovery match; Duarte 2012 & Johnson 2009 response-threshold set-point; Crall 2018 & Middleton 2016 collective response/resilience to disturbance; Khajehnejad 2023 first-principles worker inactivity)
competencies.state_required: recurrent policy memory + per-agent identity; agents hold a stable active/inactive role and re-select who is active when the target moves
competencies.state_mode: an implicit assignment of which agents are active, integrated over the count trajectory and re-formed on every set-point change or exogenous knockout

competencies.name: stigmergic coordination (environment-mediated)
competencies.description: n agents on a torus must collectively cover target cells; they cannot see each other and coordinate ONLY through marks left in a shared decaying pheromone field. First EPC competency whose coordination is externalized into the environment. Fingerprint INVERTS the role-partitioning profile: nomark (destroy the field) load-bearing 0.54, blind 0.68, while noid ~0.00 (agents interchangeable) and memwipe ~0.02 (no coordination in recurrent state) are DEAD -- the opposite of division-of-labor/size-regulation/turn-taking.
competencies.mechanism: n agents on a torus must collectively cover target cells; they cannot see each other and coordinate ONLY through marks left in a shared decaying pheromone field. First EPC competency whose coordination is externalized into the environment. Fingerprint INVERTS the role-partitioning profile: nomark (destroy the field) load-bearing 0.54, blind 0.68, while noid ~0.00 (agents interchangeable) and memwipe ~0.02 (no coordination in recurrent state) are DEAD -- the opposite of division-of-labor/size-regulation/turn-taking.
competencies.diagnostic: ablation battery incl. new nomark channel (zero the pheromone field every step): nomark necessity 0.54-0.55 across seeds (coverage drops >half), blind 0.68 load-bearing; noid 0.00-0.01 and memwipe 0.00-0.04 both irrelevant (mechanism inversion vs role-partitioning).
competencies.metric: trains 3/3 seeds to cover 0.98 (chance 0.31). internal novelty gate: min fingerprint distance 0.431 to swarm-quorum (nearest; the only other spatial-collective), above 0.4 floor; first competency outside the identity-anchored cluster.
competencies.lit_name: stigmergy / environment-mediated coordination (Grasse termite construction; Gloag 2013 review & 2016 Myxococcus; Di Caro 1998 AntNet stigmergetic routing; Hunt 2019 pheromone stigmergy in robot swarms; Talamali 2019 minimalist stigmergic foraging; Xu et al. 2019 (Xing Xu et al., OpenAlex-verified) stigmergic independent RL -- direct match)
competencies.state_required: a shared, decaying pheromone FIELD in the environment; agents deposit onto and sense it. Coordination state lives in the environment, NOT in agent memory or identity
competencies.state_mode: a spatial map of where agents have already been, held in the decaying field; steers others toward unvisited targets

competencies.lit_name: non-stationary MARL / BPR+ (Hernandez-Leal survey arXiv:1707.09183; OPS-DeMo arXiv:2406.06500)

competencies.diagnostic: novel (zero own-velocity) -> collapse
competencies.lit_name: continuous-physics MARL (Liu et al. 2019, Emergent Coordination Through Competition, arXiv:1902.07151)

competencies.name: morphology-conditioned specialization
competencies.description: specialize on the food type matching own body morphology (not by identity index)
competencies.mechanism: condition action on OWN morphology; SECOND budget-artifact correction; distinct from identity-based division-of-labor
competencies.diagnostic: nobody (zero own body one-hot) -> collapse; noid does NOT collapse

competencies.name: compositional attention (joint conditioning)
competencies.description: condition on TWO orthogonal own-state channels at once: own-morphology AND opponent-switch
competencies.mechanism: joint conditioning on two simultaneously-necessary channels; emerges only under a Transformer policy (attention over obs-history, memwipe 0.0)
competencies.diagnostic: nobody -> partial collapse AND freezeblock -> partial collapse (both necessary)
competencies.metric: 3 seeds@8000it: nobody 0.552, freezeblock 0.324 (mean; both clear 0.3 floor, 2/3 seeds clear both)
competencies.lit_name: attention-based compositional MARL policies; transformer-vs-recurrent POMDP memory (Esslinger et al. 2022 arXiv:2206.01078; Parisotto et al. 2020; Ni et al. 2023 NeurIPS)

learner_boundaries.name: mixed-motive cooperation (reciprocity in social dilemmas)
learner_boundaries.description: reciprocal cooperation in an iterated social dilemma
learner_boundaries.mechanism: independent PPO defects (V~0.20); LOLA opponent-shaping reaches tit-for-tat (V~0.99, 8 seeds zero variance)
learner_boundaries.diagnostic: resolved by a learner that shapes the co-learner's gradient (LOLA), not by more capacity

learner_boundaries.name: periodic synchronization (collective phase-locking)
learner_boundaries.description: collective timing / phase-locking across agents with heterogeneous frequencies
learner_boundaries.mechanism: independent learner (coupling K=0) fails; coupled-oscillator dynamics required (Kuramoto)
learner_boundaries.diagnostic: resolved by inter-agent coupling in the learner, not by more training
learner_boundaries.metric: order parameter climbs monotonically only with coupling on

learner_boundaries.name: one-channel necessity budget (recurrent bottleneck)
learner_boundaries.description: a recurrent (GRU) policy holds ~one necessary own-state channel and drops the other; attention breaks the budget
learner_boundaries.mechanism: two simultaneously-necessary conditionings compete for one recurrent hidden vector; a Transformer routes over observation history and holds both (this is the boundary complement of competency #30)
learner_boundaries.diagnostic: resolved by swapping GRU->Transformer with world held fixed; auxiliary loss can STEER which channel loads under GRU but not hold both
learner_boundaries.metric: GRU: one channel >=0.3, other <=0; Transformer: both ~0.32-0.55
learner_boundaries.lit_name: transformer-vs-recurrent POMDP memory (Esslinger et al. 2022 arXiv:2206.01078; Parisotto et al. 2020 GTrXL; Ni et al. 2023 NeurIPS; POPGym Morad et al. 2023)
